problem_motivation.content: There is a high demand for novel metallic alloys that combine strength, ductility, and low cost for high-temperature applications, specifically outperforming current Ni-based alloys.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The requirements for designing novel metallic alloys that are capable of surpassing a whole set of specific properties of currently available commercial alloys are, at present, a subject of high demand in the industry.

problem_motivation.content: Refractory alloys often suffer from brittleness, particularly at room temperature, which is a major challenge.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The main challenge in dealing with refractory alloys is that they are often brittle [ [12] , [13] , [14] ], especially at room temperature.

problem_motivation.content: Long milling times can cause contamination of powders with carbon and oxygen, creating a need to balance microstructural refinement with contamination avoidance.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, it was previously shown that such long times of mechanical alloying may cause contamination of the powders with C and O

prior_approach.content: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are commonly produced using liquid state methods such as vacuum arc-melting or induction melting.
prior_approach.evidence_span: HEAs are widely produced by liquid state methods, such as casting by vacuum arc-melting, induction melting, etc.

prior_limitation.content: Liquid state processing for refractory alloys is challenging and costly due to high melting temperatures, leading to element segregation.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, for refractory alloys, these production routes may become challenging and costly, as these alloys possess very high melting temperatures. Thus, segregation of certain high-melting temperature elements may occur, as for the evaporation of low melting ones.

prior_limitation.content: The powder metallurgy method, while offering solid-state processing, is highly susceptible to contamination, making oxide/carbide formation nearly unavoidable.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: On the other hand, the method is highly susceptible to contamination, and therefore the formation of oxides/carbides is nearly unavoidable, even when one uses controlled atmospheres

prior_limitation.content: Liquid phase routes such as arc-melting result in significantly lower hardness values and coarser microstructures compared to powder metallurgy.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: liquid routes such as arc-melting, which show significantly lower values for similar refractory HEAs

rejected_alternative.content: The authors avoided continuous milling to prevent system overheating and oxide formation, instead choosing a cycling scheme with idle time.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: This cycling scheme was chosen to avoid overheating of the system, and therefore to avoid any formation of potential oxides caused by the overheating of the milling jar.

rejected_alternative.content: The authors explicitly did not mill the sample for 0 hours (it was only blended), establishing this as a distinct condition rather than a standard milling process.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: The selected milling times were 0 (these were not milled, rather simply mixed together in a horizontal blender for 10 min for homogeneous blending)

causal_claim.content: Millling time is identified as a significant factor influencing the contamination level of the sintered materials.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Milling time seems to play a significant role in the contamination level of the sintered materials.

causal_claim.content: The maximum penetration depth is directly influenced by the feedstock powder milling time, which subsequently affects material hardness.
causal_claim.evidence_span: where the maximum penetration depth of the produced RHEA bulks is directly related to the time of milling of the feedstock powders, thus influencing the hardness of the materials.

causal_claim.content: Increased milling time leads to a higher fraction of ZrC formation after sintering due to contamination.
causal_claim.evidence_span: increased milling times of the powders lead to the formation of a higher fraction of ZrC after sintering

mechanism_principle.content: The increase in hardness and elastic modulus is attributed to severe plastic deformation causing reduced particle size and refined microstructures.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is a direct consequence of the severe plastic deformation caused by the prolonged mechanical milling, which results in a rise in hardness proportionally with the time of milling

mechanism_principle.content: The enhancement of mechanical properties is attributed to the Hall-Petch strengthening effect from fine-grained microstructures.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: due to the possible Hall–Petch strengthening effect

mechanism_principle.content: The absence of the HCP phase in bulk alloys is attributed to fast cooling after sintering preventing its formation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The absence of HCP on the bulk RHEAs may be explained by the relatively fast cooling after sintering, which in turn prevented its formation

hypothesis_statement.content: Ten hours of milling is hypothesized to be the optimal duration for balancing microstructural homogeneity and refinement, high hardness, and minimal contamination.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Ten hours of milling seems sufficient for achieving an optimal equilibrium between microstructural homogeneity and refinement, high hardness and minimal contamination.

hypothesis_statement.content: The variation of powder metallurgy parameters, specifically milling time, is expected to greatly affect the final microstructure and properties of the RHEA materials.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The variation in the milling time on the powders may greatly affect the final materials.

hypothesis_statement.content: The contamination levels (oxides, carbides) resulting from milling could potentially contribute positively to the material strength.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: These could potentially positively contribute to the strength of the material

evidence_result.content: Carbide formation was experimentally observed in the sintered bulks after just 3 hours of powder milling.
evidence_result.evidence_span: carbide formation was detected in the sintered bulks as early as after 3 h of powder milling

evidence_result.content: Oxides were experimentally observed after 30 hours of milling, attributed to wear of the high-carbon steel milling media.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Oxides were observed after 30 h due to wear of the high-carbon steel milling media and SPS consolidation.

evidence_result.content: The alloy milled for 50 hours exhibits the highest hardness, while the 3-hour milled alloy exhibits the lowest.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The RHEA produced by mechanical alloying of powders for a period of 50 h presented the highest hardness of 675.7 ± 9.8 HV0.2 among all alloys, while the lowest hardness of 592.9 ± 21.0 HV0.2 was exhibited by the alloy produced with the minimum milling time of 3 h.

evidence_result.content: Hardness increase correlates with milling time as penetration depth decreases under constant force.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Under the same applied force of 100 mN, the lowest hardness is related to the highest penetration depths, and it is shown by the alloy produced by milling for 3 h. With increasing milling times, the hardness proportionally increases and the penetration depths decrease.

evidence_result.content: Sintered alloys produced with 50h milling show approximately 14% higher hardness than those produced with 3h milling.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The sintered alloy corresponding to 50 h of mechanical alloying exhibits approximately 14% higher hardness than the alloy produced with 3 h of milling

evidence_result.content: The elastic modulus of sintered bulks increased by 3% with increasing milling times.
evidence_result.evidence_span: while the elastic modulus of the sintered bulks increased by 3% with increasing milling times

constraint.content: One must select milling parameters to avoid unnecessarily long times that cause contamination while achieving the desired microstructure.
constraint.evidence_span: Therefore, one must compromise and select parameters that avoid unnecessarily long milling times while achieving an appropriate microstructure

contradiction.content: Unlike previous reports or predictions, the B8_2 phase was not detected in the current alloys despite being predicted and reported in similar systems.
contradiction.evidence_span: This phase, however, was not detected in our alloys

contradiction.content: Unlike predictions and reports in other studies, the B2 phase did not transform into Ti2AlZr or Al3Zr5 in these alloys.
contradiction.evidence_span: None of these phases were found in our alloys, and neither were they predicted by CALPHAD
